title: Reserve headroom & scaling orchestration safeguards for Dedicated pools (incident response & remediation)
creator: Amaya Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-27 we observed sustained SLO violations on several Dedicated pools caused by an interaction between the predictive autoscaler (predictive-autoscaler v2) and recent kernel-selection changes. The autoscaler over-committed GPU headroom because recent telemetry changes underreported active inflight KV cache entries. This ticket captures the immediate incident response steps, short-term mitigations, and a prioritized set of long-term safeguards to prevent recurrence.
postmortem_findings: 1) Telemetry regression: an instrumentation change in the KV cache module removed per-shard inflight counters used by the autoscaler estimator. 2) Predictive model drift: predictive-autoscaler v2 parameters were tuned on pre-1.21 telemetry and produced optimistic forecasts under higher sequence-length variance. 3) Orchestration mismatch: the placement controller allowed fractional pool packing which, combined with the optimistic forecasts, caused transient overcommit and headroom exhaustion. 4) Alerting gap: no dedicated alert for sustained headroom deficit (10m at >70% pool contention) existed prior to the incident.
immediate_mitigation:
- Rolled back predictive-autoscaler to v1.9 (disabled v2) at 2026-02-27T18:22Z.
- Temporarily increased reserved headroom to +30% on impacted Dedicated pools to restore SLOs.
- Applied hotfix to restore KV cache inflight counters and deployed telemetry patch (PR #8341) to staging and prod within 2 hours.
- Enabled emergency throttles for non-critical customers on affected pools to reduce surge pressure.
action_items: (A) Short-term: Add a safe-mode flag to the autoscaler that enforces minimum headroom (default 20%) and can be toggled from Console – owner: Diego – target: 2026-03-12
(B) Observability: Reintroduce and harden per-shard inflight KV metrics + add Grafana dashboard panel 'dedicated_pool/headroom_deficit' – owner: Priya Patel – target: 2026-03-08
(C) Alerts: Create a composite alert rule for sustained headroom deficit >10 minutes AND pool throttle rate >5% – owner: SRE – target: 2026-03-05
(D) Autoscaler: Add canary rollout gating for predictive-autoscaler versions (automated rollback on headroom regression) – owner: Infra ML – RFC by 2026-03-15
(E) Orchestration: Prevent fractional packing policy on critical pools; require minimum whole-GPU headroom reservation – owner: Placement Team – target: 2026-03-18
(F) Postmortem: Draft long-form postmortem, include timeline, blast radius, customer list, and RCA; circulate for review – owner: Amaya – target: 2026-03-10
(G) Runbook: Update dedicated capacity runbook to include a step for rolling back autoscaler versions and emergency headroom injection – owner: Oncall Runbook WG – target: 2026-03-14
acceptance_criteria: Can toggle safe-mode headroom flag from Console and it immediately affects new scaling decisions
Grafana dashboard shows per-shard inflight KV metrics + dedicated_pool/headroom_deficit panel populated for production pools
New alert fires in staging and oncall pages are validated within 24h
Canary gating prevents predictive v2 rollout to >5% of capacity without explicit engineer override
Runbook contains clear rollback steps, owners, and post-incident checklist
rollout_plan: 1) Merge telemetry and autoscaler safe-mode changes behind feature flags. 2) Deploy telemetry patch to prod (already done) and validate metrics for 24h. 3) Enable safe-mode in a single low-risk pool for 2h, observe headroom and latency. 4) If stable, expand safe-mode to all critical Dedicated pools. 5) Enforce canary gating on the CI/CD pipeline for predictive-autoscaler releases and block any rollout that increases headroom deficit by >10% in staging.
runbook_updates: Add 'rollback predictive-autoscaler' section with CLI commands and Console toggles
Document 'emergency headroom injection' procedure and required approvals
Add troubleshooting checklist for headroom vs. KV-cache telemetry discrepancies
